Acne: It is acne. Use benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid. Keep skin clean and avoid picking. Consult a dermatologist for severe cases.
Contact Dermatitis: It is contact dermatitis. Avoid the irritant/allergen. Use topical corticosteroids and moisturizers. If severe, consult a dermatologist.
Eczema: It is eczema. Atopic dermatitis with dry, itchy skin. Use moisturizer and topical corticosteroids. Avoid harsh soaps and irritants.
Fungal Infection: It is a fungal infection. Use antifungal cream. Keep area clean and dry. If no improvement, consult a dermatologist.
Herpes: It is herpes. Use antiviral medication. Avoid touching the area. Consult a dermatologist for proper treatment.
Insect Bite Dermatitis: It is insect bite dermatitis. Apply cold compress. Use antihistamines and hydrocortisone cream. Watch for signs of infection.
Lichen Planus: It is lichen planus. Use topical corticosteroids. If widespread, consult a dermatologist for systemic treatment.
Miliaria: It is miliaria (heat rash). Keep cool and dry. Use calamine lotion. Avoid excessive sweating.
Palmoplantar Keratoderma: It is palmoplantar keratoderma. Use emollients and keratolytic agents. Consult a dermatologist for advanced treatment.
Papular Urticaria: It is papular urticaria. Avoid insect bites. Use antihistamines and topical corticosteroids. Consult a dermatologist for persistent cases.
Psoriasis: It is psoriasis. Use topical steroids and moisturizers. Phototherapy may help. Consult a dermatologist for systemic treatment.
Purpura: It is purpura. Consult a doctor immediately. This may indicate a bleeding disorder or vasculitis.
Rosacea: It is rosacea. Use gentle skincare. Avoid triggers like spicy food and alcohol. Consult a dermatologist for prescription treatment.
Seborrheic Dermatitis: It is seborrheic dermatitis. Use antifungal shampoo. Apply topical corticosteroids. If scalp, use medicated shampoos.
Urticaria: It is urticaria (hives). Use antihistamines. Avoid triggers. If chronic, consult a dermatologist.
